1.q: וְ⁠אֶת־בֵּית⁠וֹ֙ בָּנָ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה שְׁלֹ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה וַ⁠יְכַ֖ל אֶת־כָּל־בֵּיתֽ⁠וֹ
1.note: In this verse, the author is introducing a new event in the story, Solomon building his **house** or palace. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

1.q: וְ⁠אֶת־בֵּית⁠וֹ֙ בָּנָ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה שְׁלֹ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה וַ⁠יְכַ֖ל אֶת־כָּל־בֵּיתֽ⁠וֹ
1.note: Together, the verbs **built** and **finished** express a single idea. The word **finished** tells to what degree Solomon **built** his palace over the course of these 13 years, that is, to completion. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [And then Solomon took 13 years to finish building his house] or [And Solomon completed constructing his palace after a further 13 years]
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:26. Alternate translation: [And Solomon had his workers build]

The term **house** in this chapter usually refers to Solomon’s entire palace complex, which included the House of the Forest of Lebanon (7:2–5), the Porch of Pillars (7:6), the Porch of the Throne (7:7), Solomon’s personal residence (7:8), and the surrounding courtyard (7:12). However, in (7:8) the author refers to Solomon’s residence itself as his “house.” So you may wish to use a term other than “house” in your translation to refer to the entire complex. Alternate translation: [his palace]

2.note: This was not a **House** in which anyone lived. It was a great ceremonial hall in which Solomon kept his collection of shields and weapons. Solomon may also have hosted large public assemblies and royal ceremonies in this hall. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a term other than “house” to describe this building. Alternate translation: [the Forest of Lebanon Hall]

2.q: מֵאָ֨ה אַמָּ֤ה & וַ⁠חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ & וּ⁠שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אַמָּ֖ה
2.note: See the discussion of the term “cubits” in the introduction to chapter 6, and see how you decided to describe the lengths that the author expresses in cubits in that chapter.

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [The structure rested upon]

3.note: The expression **it was covered** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And cedar covered it] or [And the workers covered it with cedar]

3.q: הָֽ⁠עַמּוּדִ֔ים אַרְבָּעִ֖ים וַ⁠חֲמִשָּׁ֑ה חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר הַ⁠טּֽוּר
3.note: The author is using the phrase **15 the row** as a common expression of his culture to mean that there were 15 **pillars** in each **row** that he is describing. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [45 pillars that were in rows of 15]

5.note: The phrase **entrances and doorposts** expresses a single idea, that these **entrances** were framed by these **doorposts**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [the entrances framed by the doorposts were square]

6.note: This building had a name that used the same term that the author uses to describe the “porch” of the temple in 6:3. That suggests that this building was located just outside the House of the Forest of Lebanon. (The fact that its length was equal to the width of that building supports this idea.) It probably served as a ceremonial entranceway for that building. However, this building also had a **porch** of its own. So if it would be clearer in your language, you could use a name for this building as a whole that uses a term other than “porch.” Alternate translation: [the Colonnade of Pillars]

The author seems to be using the pronoun **their** to refer to the **Pillars** of this entryway. He is using those pillars to represent the entire building, whose most prominent feature they were. Alternate translation: [And a porch was on the face of this building, and pillars and a roof were on its face]

Here, **face** represents the front of the building. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And a porch was in front of it, and pillars and a roof were in front of it]

It might seem that repeating the phrase **on their face** would be extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could represent this phrase only once. Alternate translation: [And a porch with pillars and a roof was in front of it]

7.note: This building was known by two names that each used the same term that describes the “porch” of the temple in 6:3. However, it is clear that this building was not a mere entrance. It was a formal hall in which Solomon judged cases. So if it would be clearer in your language, you could use a name for this building that uses a term other than “porch.” Alternate translation: [the Hall of the Throne … the Hall of Judgment]

It might seem that the expression **where he would judge there** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it, here and in verse 8. Alternate translation: [where he would judge]

The author is using **from the floor to the floor** as a common expression of his culture to mean “over the entire floor.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And its entire floor was covered with cedar]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:3. Alternate translation: [And cedar covered its entire floor] or [And the workers covered its entire floor with cedar]

8.note: The author calls this the **other courtyard** to distinguish it from the temple courtyard that he describes in 6:36. He describes the construction of this courtyard in 7:12. You could indicate this distinction explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in the palace courtyard]

By **the house of the porch**, the author seems to mean the building most recently mentioned that had the word “porch” in its name, which would be the Porch of the Throne (the Porch of Judgment). Alternate translation: [from the Porch of the Throne]

The author is using the term **from** to mean that Solomon’s residence was a separate building within the palace complex from the Porch of the Throne and the two buildings that adjoined it. Alternate translation: [set back from the Porch of the Throne] or [away from the Porch of the Throne and its adjoining buildings]

The author means that the work that Solomon’s builders did to construct his residence was **like** the **work** they did to construct the Porch of the Throne (and its adjoining buildings). This seems to refer to the materials they used, their method of construction, and the architectural style and details. It does not seem to be a description of the size of Solomon’s residence. (The author does not give its dimensions.) Alternate translation: [was of similar construction to the Porch of the Throne]

8.q: וּ⁠בַ֜יִת יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה לְ⁠בַת־פַּרְעֹה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָקַ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה
8.note: The pronoun **whom** refers to the daughter of Pharaoh, while the pronoun **he** refers to Solomon. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And he made a house for the daughter of Pharaoh, whom he had taken]
As in the first instance earlier in the verse, here the term **porch** seems to refer to the Porch of the Throne. Alternate translation: [of similar construction to the Porch of the Throne]

9.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [All of these buildings were built with valuable stones]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:17. Alternate translation: [were built with high-quality limestone blocks]

The author is not referring to a specific **saw**. He means saws in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [sawn with saws]

The author is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [trimmed with saws]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the stonework extended from the foundation to the eaves]

The author is speaking as if the stonework of the palace buildings extended from them to the **great courtyard** that was **outside** of them. He means that the wall of the great courtyard had stones and workmanship of the same quality as those in the buildings it surrounded. The author does not mean that the entire courtyard was paved with stones. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the workers used the same kind of stonework to build the wall of the great courtyard outside]

10.note: The expression **it was founded** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And he founded it with valuable stones] or [And its foundation consisted of valuable stones]

12.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Its wall consisted of three rows of hewn stone]

If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [just as for the inner courtyard of the house of Yahweh]
See how you translated the similar expression in [3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]

13.q: וַ⁠יִּשְׁלַח֙ הַ⁠מֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַ⁠יִּקַּ֥ח אֶת־חִירָ֖ם מִ⁠צֹּֽר
13.note: Here and in the next verse, the author is introducing this man named **Hiram** as a new participant in the story. This is not the same man by that name who was the king of Tyre, whose friendship with Solomon the author describes in chapter 5. If your language has its own way of introducing new participants, you could use it here in your translation. Alternate translation: [And King Solomon sent and took a certain man named Hiram from Tyre]

14.q: בֶּן־אִשָּׁה֩ אַלְמָנָ֨ה ה֜וּא מִ⁠מַּטֵּ֣ה נַפְתָּלִ֗י וְ⁠אָבִ֣י⁠ו אִישׁ־צֹרִי֮ חֹרֵ֣שׁ נְחֹשֶׁת֒
14.note: The author is describing Hiram’s parents as he continues to introduce him as a new participant in the story. Introduce Hiram’s parents in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [He was the son of a certain woman from the tribe of Naphtali. His father, who had passed away, was a certain man who had lived in Tyre and had been a crafter of bronze]

The author is speaking as if Hiram had been a container that these qualities **filled**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And he had been given wisdom and understanding and knowledge]

The expression **was filled** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And God had filled him with wisdom and understanding and knowledge] or [And God had given him wisdom and understanding and knowledge]

The terms **wisdom** and **understanding** and **knowledge** mean similar things. The author is using these three terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [And God had given him very great skill] or [And he had very great skill]

The author is saying **all of his work** as a generalization for emphasis. He means specifically that Hiram did all of the work that Solomon asked him to do. If it would be clearer in your language, you could express the emphasis in a different way. Alternate translation: [and he did all the work that Solomon asked him to do]

15.q: שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֜ה אַמָּ֗ה קוֹמַת֙ הָ⁠עַמּ֣וּד הָ⁠אֶחָ֔ד וְ⁠חוּט֙ שְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אַמָּ֔ה יָסֹ֖ב אֶת־הָ⁠עַמּ֥וּד הַ⁠שֵּׁנִֽי
15.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [18 cubits was the height of the one pillar, and 18 cubits was the height of the second pillar. A cord of 12 cubits surrounded the one pillar, and cord of 12 cubits surrounded the second pillar] or [18 cubits was the height of each pillar, and a cord of 12 cubits surrounded each pillar]

15.q: וְ⁠חוּט֙ שְׁתֵּים־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אַמָּ֔ה יָסֹ֖ב אֶת־הָ⁠עַמּ֥וּד הַ⁠שֵּׁנִֽי
15.note: The author is not saying that there was such a **cord** around this **pillar** all the time. He is indicating what the circumference of the pillar was, by reference to how someone in his culture would measure that circumference. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the second pillar was 12 cubits in circumference] or [and the measurement of the distance around the second pillar was 12 cubits]

See the discussion of the term “second” in the introduction to chapter 6, and see how you decided to represent that term in your translation throughout that chapter. Alternate translation: [the other pillar] or [pillar number two]

16.note: These **capitals** were a kind of decorative top piece that was placed on top of pillars or columns. If your readers would not be familiar with what a capital is, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [decorative tops] or [ornamental tops]

The author is using the term **heads** to mean the tops of these **pillars**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly, here and in the next verse. Alternate translation: [the tops of the pillars]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [They were casting of bronze] or [They were bronze castings]

16.q: חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֗וֹת קוֹמַת֙ הַ⁠כֹּתֶ֣רֶת הָ⁠אֶחָ֔ת וְ⁠חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֔וֹת קוֹמַ֖ת הַ⁠כֹּתֶ֥רֶת הַ⁠שֵּׁנִֽית
16.note: It might seem that this expression contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it, here and in verses 17 and 18. Alternate translation: [Five cubits was the height of each capital]

17.q: שְׂבָכִ֞ים מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה שְׂבָכָ֗ה גְּדִלִים֙ מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה שַׁרְשְׁר֔וֹת לַ⁠כֹּ֣תָרֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָ⁠עַמּוּדִ֑ים
17.note: This could mean: (1) that Hiram covered the capitals with decorative bronze **netting** and that he made the **strands** of the netting by twisting bronze wires together, as one would do to make **chains** (not in the sense of chains composed of separate links, but in the sense of a strong cord). Alternate translation: [The capitals on top of the pillars had decorative netting made from bronze that had been formed into thick strands, as for chains] or (2) that Hiram covered the capitals with decorative bronze netting and then draped chains over the netting that he had made by twisting bronze into thick strands. Alternate translation: [The capitals on top of the pillars had for decoration bronze netting and chains made of strands of twisted bronze]

In this verse, the word **head** is singular in form, but it refers to all the tops of the pillars as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “head,” here and in verses 18, 19, and 22. Alternate translation: [the heads of the pillars] or [the tops of the pillars]

18.note: Some ancient manuscripts read “And he made pillars” and “the head of the pomegranates.” The ULT follows those readings. Other ancient manuscripts read “And he made pomegranates” and “the head of the pillars.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

18.q: וַ⁠יַּ֖עַשׂ אֶת־הָ⁠עַמּוּדִ֑ים וּ⁠שְׁנֵי֩ טוּרִ֨ים סָבִ֜יב עַל־הַ⁠שְּׂבָכָ֣ה הָ⁠אֶחָ֗ת לְ⁠כַסּ֤וֹת אֶת־הַ⁠כֹּֽתָרֹת֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָֽ⁠רִמֹּנִ֔ים וְ⁠כֵ֣ן עָשָׂ֔ה לַ⁠כֹּתֶ֖רֶת הַ⁠שֵּׁנִֽית
18.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the purpose of the pomegranates (**to cover the capitals**) right after the statement that Hiram **made** them. Alternate translation: [And he made pomegranates to cover the capitals that were on the head of the pillars, and two rows all around on one network, and thus he did for the second capital]

If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [with two rows all around each network]

In this verse, the word **network** is singular in form, but it refers to all networks as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “network” or a plural expression, here and in verses 20, 41, and 42. Alternate translation: [networks] or [set of networks]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Thus he did for the first capital, and thus he did for the second capital] or [Thus he did for each capital]

19.q: וְ⁠כֹֽתָרֹ֗ת אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָ⁠עַמּוּדִ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה שׁוּשַׁ֣ן בָּֽ⁠אוּלָ֑ם
19.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the **porch** with the information about the **pillars**. Alternate translation: [And the capitals that were on the head of the pillars on the porch were the work of a lily]

To translate the phrase **the work of** here and in its several further occurrences in the rest of this chapter, see the discussion of that phrase in the introduction to this chapter. Alternate translation: [were made in the shape of lilies]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [The lily-shaped top portion of the capitals was four cubits high]

20.q: וְ⁠כֹתָרֹ֗ת עַל־שְׁנֵי֙ הָֽ⁠עַמּוּדִ֔ים גַּם־מִ⁠מַּ֨עַל֙ מִ⁠לְּ⁠עֻמַּ֣ת הַ⁠בֶּ֔טֶן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לְ⁠עֵ֣בֶר שבכה
20.note: In the previous verse, the author described the upper part of each capital. In this verse, he describes the lower part of each capital, the part just **above** the pillars. As he specifies which part he is referring to, he provides new information about the shape of this part. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could show in your translation that he is providing new information. Alternate translation: [And as for the part of the capitals just above the two pillars, the part that was on the other side of the network, it was shaped like a belly]

The author is describing the location of this part of the **capitals** relative to the **network** of bronze strands in a way characteristic of his culture. He means that if someone were looking at the capitals, they would see the network of bronze strands, and they would see the belly-shaped lower part of the capital behind or **on the other side of** those bronze strands. Express this in the way people of your culture describe the location of one thing relative to another, or use plain language to express the meaning. Alternate translation: [that was behind the network] or [that was covered by the network]

If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [there the pomegranates]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:18. Alternate translation: [on the first capital, and also on the second capital] or [on each capital]

21.note: The author is using Hiram, whom he represents with the pronoun **he**, one person who was involved in this action, to represent everyone who was involved. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Hiram and his workers set up the pillars]
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:8. Alternate translation: [the south pillar … the north pillar]

It might seem that the expression **called its name** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [and called it Jachin] or [and named it Jachin]

22.q: וְ⁠עַ֛ל רֹ֥אשׁ הָ⁠עַמּוּדִ֖ים מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה שׁוֹשָׁ֑ן וַ⁠תִּתֹּ֖ם מְלֶ֥אכֶת הָ⁠עַמּוּדִֽים
22.note: In this verse, the author is concluding his account of how Hiram cast massive pillars with ornate capitals for the temple porch. In the first sentence, he repeats what he said in 7:19 about the lily-shaped decorations on top of the capitals. That repetition signals the impending conclusion of the account, which ends in the next sentence with the author’s statement that once the pillars were set up, the work on them was **finished**. Use a natural form in your language for concluding an account with a brief summary of what it has described.

The expression **was finished** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And Hiram finished the work of the pillars]

23.note: Here, the term **cast** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And he made a sea by casting it in bronze]

This was a very large water basin. It was called a **sea** because it contained so much water. In your translation, you could indicate explicitly what it actually was if that would be helpful to your readers. The UST models one way to do that.
To translate the expression **by the cubit** here and in the rest of this chapter, see how you translated the same expression in 6:3 and throughout chapter 6. Alternate translation: [ten cubits wide]

The author is using the term **lip** to mean the brim of this **sea**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly here and in verses 24 and 26. Alternate translation: [from one brim to the other] or [across its width]

24.note: The expressions **were cast** and **was cast** are passive verbal forms. If your language would not use such forms, you could express this idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Hiram cast the gourds when he cast the sea]

It is not clear whether the author means that there were ten gourds per cubit in each row, for a total of 600, or ten gourds per cubit in both rows, for a total of 300. Since the meaning is uncertain, try to translate these expressions in a way that allows for both possibilities. The UST models one way to do that.

25.note: In this verse, the word **cattle** is singular in form, but it refers to these 12 bronze statues of bulls. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a plural form to express this meaning here and in verses 29 and 44. Alternate translation: [bulls]

25.q: שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה פֹנִ֣ים ׀ צָפ֡וֹנָ⁠ה וּ⁠שְׁלֹשָׁה֩ פֹנִ֨ים ׀ יָ֜מָּ⁠ה וּ⁠שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה ׀ פֹּנִ֣ים נֶ֗גְבָּ⁠ה וּ⁠שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ פֹּנִ֣ים מִזְרָ֔חָ⁠ה
25.note: It might seem that repeating the phrase **three facing** four times would be extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could represent this phrase just once in your translation. Alternate translation: [which faced outward to the north, west, south, and east in groups of three]

26.note: A **handbreadth** was a unit of measurement corresponding to the width of a man’s hand measured across the palm, or about eight centimeters or about three and a half inches. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this width in modern measurements, either in the text of your translation or in a footnote.

This could mean: (1) that the shape of the **lip** or brim of the sea was like the shape of the **lip** or edge of a cup and like the shape of the **blossom of a lily**. Alternate translation: [and the brim of the sea was shaped like the edge of a cup and like the blossom of a lily] or (2) that the shape of the **lip** or brim of the sea was like the shape of the **lip** or edge of a cup and that it had decorations in the shape of the **blossom of a lily**. Alternate translation: [and the brim of the sea was shaped like the edge of a cup, and it had lily blossoms as decorations]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the lip of a cup** and **the blossom of a lily** curve outward, so the **lip** or brim of the sea curved outward. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and its brim was fashioned to curve outward, like the edge of a cup and like a lily blossom]

These **baths** were each equivalent to 22 liters or nearly six gallons. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote.

28.note: In this verse, the word **stand** is singular in form, but it refers to all the stands as a group. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the stands] or [each stand]

29.q: וְ⁠עַל־הַ⁠שְׁלַבִּ֖ים כֵּ֣ן מִ⁠מָּ֑עַל וּ⁠מִ⁠תַּ֨חַת֙ לַ⁠אֲרָי֣וֹת וְ⁠לַ⁠בָּקָ֔ר לֹי֖וֹת מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה מוֹרָֽד
29.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the **wreaths** that were below the **lions** and **cattle** in the first part of this sentence. That way it would follow directly from the author’s introduction of these decorations in the previous sentence. Alternate translation: [And from below to the lions and to the cattle were wreaths, the work of descent, and on the frames was a pedestal from above]

29.q: וּ⁠מִ⁠תַּ֨חַת֙ לַ⁠אֲרָי֣וֹת וְ⁠לַ⁠בָּקָ֔ר לֹי֖וֹת מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה מוֹרָֽד
29.note: The phrase **the work of descent** could indicate: (1) that these **wreaths** were crafted to appear as if they were hanging down from the panels. Alternate translation: [and below the lions and cattle were wreaths that appeared to hang down from the panels] or (2) that these **wreaths** were hammered or embossed onto the surface of the panels. Alternate translation: [and below the lions and cattle, wreath designs were worked into the panels]

As he did in 6:32, here the author also mentions only two of three terms he has introduced in a preceding sentence. You may wish to indicate that what he says applies to the third term as well. See what you did in 6:32. Alternate translation: [and below the lions, bulls, and cherubs]

30.q: וְ⁠אַרְבָּעָה֩ & וְ⁠אַרְבָּעָ֥ה פַעֲמֹתָ֖י⁠ו כְּתֵפֹ֣ת לָ⁠הֶ֑ם מִ⁠תַּ֤חַת לַ⁠כִּיֹּר֙
30.note: The author is using the term **shoulders** to mean supports for the **basin** that each stand held and transported. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And there were supports on the four corners of each stand to hold up a basin]

The author assumes that his readers will know that each of these stands supported a **basin** in which the priests washed the parts of animals that they would burn as sacrifices. (The parallel passage in 2 Chronicles 4:6 says this specifically.) The author therefore assumes that readers will know that by **the basin**, he means the basin that each of these stands supported. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [to the basin that the stand supported]

The expression **were cast** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Hiram decorated the side of each support with wreaths that he cast in bronze]

31.note: The pronoun translated as **its** in the first instance is masculine, so it refers to the “basin” described in the previous verse. The pronoun translated as **its** in the second and third instances is feminine, so it refers to the **capital**. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the mouth of the basin … And the mouth of the capital … the mouth of the capital]

The author is using the term **mouth** in these first two instances to mean the openings of the basin and the capital. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the opening of the basin … And the opening of the capital]

The author is using the term **capital** to describe the structure on top of the stand that he calls a **pedestal** later in this verse and in 7:29. He uses that term because the structure was placed on top of the stand, just like the decorative features on top of the pillars that he also calls “capitals” in 7:16–20. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use the term “pedestal” here instead to make clear that the author is referring to that, not to the features of the pillars. Alternate translation: [the pedestal]

See the discussion of the phrase **the work of** in the introduction to this chapter. Alternate translation: [And its mouth was circular because it was made to be a pedestal] or [And its mouth was circular so that it could serve as a pedestal]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [it was a cubit and half of a cubit across]

Here, the **mouth** or opening of the capital (pedestal) represents the rim around that opening. The author means that there were **carvings** on the rim of the pedestal, just as there were on the rim of the sea, as he describes in 7:24. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and there were also carvings around the rim of the pedestal]

The pronoun **their** refers to the bronze stands. The author is repeating a detail he described in 7:27–28 to indicate that these stands had a combination of round and square elements. Alternate translation: [But the panels of the stands were square, not round]

32.note: The author is using the term **hands** to mean axles of the wheels, which he describes in 7:30. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly, here and the next verse. Alternate translation: [and the axles of the wheels were in the stand]

When he says that the **hands of the wheels** were **in the stand**, the author means that the axles of the wheels were cast as part of the stand itself, rather than as separate pieces that were added afterwards. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the axles of the wheels were cast as part of the stand]

33.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the wheel of a chariot** is open, with **spokes** connecting the rim to the hub, so the **wheels** of these stands were open, with **spokes**, **rims**, and **hubs**. In this culture, carts designed to bear heavy loads had solid wooden wheels. The author is indicating Hiram’s skill and ingenuity in casting open metal wheels that could support the weight of the water that the basin held (900 kilograms or 2,000 pounds) in addition to the weight of the bronze basin itself and its bronze stand. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And Hiram made the wheels open, like chariot wheels, but they were still able to support the weight of the stand and its basin when it was full of water]

33.q: יְדוֹתָ֣⁠ם וְ⁠גַבֵּי⁠הֶ֗ם וְ⁠חִשֻּׁקֵי⁠הֶ֛ם וְ⁠חִשֻּׁרֵי⁠הֶ֖ם הַ⁠כֹּ֥ל מוּצָֽק
33.note: The expression **was cast** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Hiram cast every part of these wheels from bronze, including their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs]

34.q: וְ⁠אַרְבַּ֣ע כְּתֵפ֔וֹת אֶ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פִּנּ֔וֹת הַ⁠מְּכֹנָ֖ה הָֽ⁠אֶחָ֑ת מִן־הַ⁠מְּכֹנָ֖ה כְּתֵפֶֽי⁠הָ
34.note: If it would not be natural in your language to repeat the terms **four** and **shoulders**, you could shorten this description. Alternate translation: [And the shoulders that were to the four corners of one stand were from the stand] or [And the supports on the four corners of the base were cast as part of the base itself]

35.q: וּ⁠בְ⁠רֹ֣אשׁ הַ⁠מְּכוֹנָ֗ה חֲצִ֧י הָ⁠אַמָּ֛ה קוֹמָ֖ה עָגֹ֣ל ׀ סָבִ֑יב
35.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And on the head of the stand there was a pedestal, half of a cubit was its height, and it was circular all around]

As in 7:16–22, the author is using the term **head** to mean “top.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly, here and in the next verse. Alternate translation: [And on the top of each stand]

In this context, the author is probably using the term **hands** to mean support bars that held the pedestal securely in place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly, here and the next verse. Alternate translation: [its support bars]

36.note: The pronoun **he** refers to Hiram. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Hiram engraved]

36.q: עַל־הַ⁠לֻּחֹת֙ יְדֹתֶ֔י⁠הָ וְ⁠עַל֙ ו⁠מסגרתי⁠ה כְּרוּבִ֖ים אֲרָי֣וֹת וְ⁠תִמֹרֹ֑ת כְּ⁠מַֽעַר־אִ֥ישׁ וְ⁠לֹי֖וֹת סָבִֽיב
36.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the **wreaths all around** with the information about the carvings of **cherubs, lions, and palm trees**. Alternate translation: [cherubs, lions, and palm trees and wreaths all around on the plates of its hands and on its panels, according to the bare space of each]

37.note: In this verse, the author is concluding the account he gives in 7:27–37 of how Hiram cast these **ten stands** to hold and transport water basins in the temple area. Use a natural form in your language for concluding an account.

38.note: These **baths** were each equivalent to 22 liters or nearly six gallons. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote. See what you did in 7:26.

38.q: הָ⁠אֶחָ֗ד & כִּיּ֤וֹר & עַל־הַ⁠מְּכוֹנָ֣ה הָ⁠אַחַ֔ת לְ⁠עֶ֖שֶׂר הַ⁠מְּכֹנֽוֹת
38.note: It might seem that this expression contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [One basin was on each of the ten stands]

39.q: עַל־כֶּ֤תֶף הַ⁠בַּ֨יִת֙ מִ⁠יָּמִ֔ין & כֶּ֥תֶף הַ⁠בַּ֖יִת מִ⁠שְּׂמֹאל֑⁠וֹ
39.note: As in 6:8, the author is using the term **shoulder** to mean the side of the **house** or temple. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in front of the right side of the temple … in front of the left side of the temple]

39.q: עַל־כֶּ֤תֶף הַ⁠בַּ֨יִת֙ מִ⁠יָּמִ֔ין & כֶּ֥תֶף הַ⁠בַּ֖יִת מִ⁠שְּׂמֹאל֑⁠וֹ
39.note: See the discussion in a note to 6:8 of how, in these descriptions of the temple, the author is speaking of directions in the way that is characteristic of his culture. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could indicate the directions he is speaking of, particularly since he uses the terms **eastward** and **south** later in the verse. Alternate translation: [in front of the south side of the temple … in front of the north side of the temple]

39.q: מִ⁠כֶּ֨תֶף הַ⁠בַּ֧יִת הַ⁠יְמָנִ֛ית קֵ֖דְמָ⁠ה מִ⁠מּ֥וּל נֶֽגֶב
39.note: By **from the right shoulder of the house, eastward toward the south**, the author means at the southeast corner of the temple. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in front of the southeast corner of the temple]

40.note: Some ancient manuscripts read “basins.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “pots,” as in the summary in 7:45. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

40.q: וַ⁠יְכַ֣ל חִירָ֗ם לַֽ⁠עֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַ⁠מְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה לַ⁠מֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה
40.note: Beginning with this sentence and continuing through the next five verses, the author concludes his entire account in 7:13–40 of how Hiram made many types of bronze items for Yahweh’s temple. In the next five verses, he gives a summary of all the items, and in this sentence, he introduces that summary. Use a natural form in your language for introducing the conclusion of an account that summarizes what it has described.

41.note: The author is using the possessive form to describe **capitals** that were in the shape of **bowls**. (This refers to the bottom part of the capitals, as 7:20 indicates.) If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the bowl-shaped capitals]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:16. Alternate translation: [the tops of the two pillars]

42.note: The author is using the term **faces** to mean the tops of these **pillars**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the tops of the pillars]

44.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 7:25. Alternate translation: [the 12 bulls]

45.note: Here, the term **polished** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [were bronze that workers polished after Hiram cast them]

46.note: The author is using **the king** (Solomon, who directed this action) to represent everyone who was involved. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Hiram and his workers cast them, as the king had commissioned them to do]

The author is using the possessive form to describe **ground** that consists largely of **clay**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in the clayey ground]

47.note: The author is speaking of these **vessels** as if they had been living things that could **rest**. (He is speaking as if weighing the vessels would have caused them some exertion.) If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Solomon did not weigh the vessels]

The author is repeating the word **great** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [because Hiram used such a great abundance of bronze to make them]

The expression **was not determined** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [No one determined the weight of the bronze]

48.q: וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠שֻּׁלְחָ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלָ֛י⁠ו לֶ֥חֶם הַ⁠פָּנִ֖ים זָהָֽב
48.note: The author specifies that this **table** was made of **gold** after describing the table itself in order to emphasize that it was made from that precious metal. If it would be more natural in your language, here and in the next two verses, you could use the adjective “golden” within the description of the articles themselves to provide the information that these vessels for the house of Yahweh were made of gold. Alternate translation: [and the golden table that had the bread of the face on it]

Here, the term **face** represents the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [was the Bread of the Presence]

49.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the five lampstands]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the inner sanctuary. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in front of]

In this verse, the word **blossom** is singular in form, but it refers to all the floral decorations as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “blossom” or an equivalent term. Alternate translation: [and the blossoms] or [and the flowers]

The author assumes that readers will know that the golden lampstand in the sacred tent had decorations of flowers, and so Solomon had his workers make **lampstands** of a similar design for the temple. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the floral designs on the lampstands]

50.note: The author is using the term **palms** to mean some implement that the priests used in the temple area that had a cupped shape. This could mean: (1) Alternate translation: [incense dishes] or (2) Alternate translation: [spoons] or [ladles]
